rule: No PCV-03A runtime implementation may begin until PCV-I01..PCV-I06 complete in strict order. Every finding must have an owner, disposition, dependency/consumer mapping, and validation route; unresolved owner/authority/contract gaps block I06.

findings.title: Parallel Campaign membership authority.
findings.detail: `pcv03Session.ts` mints and persists `Pcv03Membership` while also mutating PCV-02 `memberSubjectIds`. This bypasses the canonical A5 Campaign membership/invitation owner instead of adapting it.

findings.title: Join is not A3 invitation acceptance.
findings.detail: PCV-03 compares `invitationId + raw secret` directly, then creates membership itself. A3's lifecycle semantics—recipient binding, one-time/idempotent acceptance, decline, revoke, inference-safe preview—are not composed.

findings.title: Accepted invitation remains reusable.
findings.detail: PCV-03 writes `acceptedSubjectId` but never checks it before later acceptance. The same invitation secret can be presented again by another subject/device.

findings.title: Peer is not bound to the joined subject.
findings.detail: After a data channel opens, `command.actorId` and presence `subjectId/deviceId` remain caller-supplied. Authorization is evaluated using the claimed actor rather than the authenticated/bound connection identity. A connected member can therefore attempt to act as another active member.

findings.title: Resume authorization is hard-coded current.
findings.detail: `acceptPcv03Resume` calls the reconnect contract with `membershipActive:true` and `permissionCurrent:true` rather than rechecking current membership/authorization.

findings.title: Resume device is not validated against registered device continuity.
findings.detail: A valid subject/resume token/epoch can supply a different `deviceId`; the handler does not prove that device is an already-authorized continuity device.

findings.title: No Campaign membership state transition seam is consumed.
findings.detail: A5 models `active | suspended | left | removed`, but PCV-03 cannot observe/enforce those states through its local membership copy. Revocation/suspension cannot reliably terminate live/resume authority.

findings.title: Supported role vocabulary is not explicitly adapted.
findings.detail: A5 uses `game-master/assistant-gm/content-creator`; the older Campaign authorization policy uses `gm/player/observer`. PCV-03 currently uses only player/observer but has no explicit fail-closed translation seam for future A5 roles.

findings.title: PCV-03 creates a parallel Session owner.
findings.detail: It creates `Pcv03HostSession` directly from PCV-02 Campaign/Scene state rather than consuming the canonical A5 launched Session shell / immutable launch snapshot.

findings.title: Paused/closed Session state is not enforced.
findings.detail: PCV-03 join, resume, command, and presence paths have no A5 `launched | paused | closed` gate.

findings.title: Old Sessions remain addressable.
findings.detail: Starting a new host changes the `active-host` pointer but does not close the old Session or revoke its invitations/resume credentials. Old records can continue accepting traffic if addressed directly.

findings.title: Session replacement/closure does not advance authority epoch or revoke credentials.
findings.detail: The authority epoch is initialized to 1 and never participates in a real lifecycle transition.

findings.title: Selected Campaign context is ignored when hosting.
findings.detail: `ensurePcv03CampaignContext` returns the first Campaign in the foundation rather than the user's selected Campaign context.

findings.title: Remote joined Campaign continuity is not integrated into ordinary product context.
findings.detail: The player retains a PCV-03 continuity record, but the joined remote Campaign/Session is not represented as a role-safe selected-context/Home projection after restart.

findings.title: Client continuity key is only `subjectId`.
findings.detail: Multiple Campaign/Session continuities for one subject collide instead of being keyed by authoritative Campaign/Session identity.

findings.title: PCV-03 accepts arbitrary command types/payloads.
findings.detail: Any `SessionCommand.type` and arbitrary payload can enter the generic authoritative handler. PCV-03 should expose only its bounded session-continuity/proof command schema; PCV-04 owns gameplay/action convergence.

findings.title: Conflicting idempotency reuse is not detected.
findings.detail: Reusing a processed `commandId` returns the prior receipt even if the new command type/payload differs. No payload fingerprint binds idempotency identity to semantics.

findings.title: Client timestamp becomes authoritative Event time.
findings.detail: The generic handler uses `command.submittedAt` for `occurredAt`; PCV-03 passes the phone-supplied timestamp through instead of stamping host-authoritative receipt time.

findings.title: Ordered transport does not serialize asynchronous host mutations.
findings.detail: The data channel is ordered, but each received envelope launches an independent async task. Two rapid commands can overlap reads/writes and race the compare-and-swap store.

findings.title: Cross-owner join mutation is non-atomic.
findings.detail: PCV-03 mutates the PCV-02 Campaign member list before persisting its own Session membership. A later save conflict/failure can leave the two records inconsistent.

findings.title: Join acceptance advances the player's acknowledged Event cursor before delivery.
findings.detail: `join-accepted.lastSequence` is stored as `lastAcknowledgedSequence` before the subsequent Event batch is actually received.

findings.title: Command ACK advances the Event cursor before Event delivery.
findings.detail: The ACK's host `lastSequence` is written into the client recovery cursor before the Event batch arrives. A disconnect between ACK and batch can cause reconnect to skip an Event permanently.

findings.title: Client Event merge does not perform gap detection.
findings.detail: Incoming Events are deduplicated/sorted by ID/sequence, but the canonical ordered-delivery reducer is not used to detect gaps or trigger authoritative recovery.

findings.title: Visible Events and authoritative stream cursor are conflated.
findings.detail: Hidden-before-publication filtering can legitimately omit global sequence numbers. PCV-03 needs an explicit authoritative durable cursor separate from the visible Event list so secrecy does not look like loss and loss does not look like secrecy.

findings.title: Checkpoint never rolls forward.
findings.detail: The only checkpoint is created at Session start; later commands/events never create or advance a checkpoint lifecycle.

findings.title: Checkpoint checksum is not integrity evidence.
findings.detail: The value is a predictable label (`pcv03-checkpoint:<campaign>:1:1`) and reconnect compares the checkpoint's value to itself. There is no separately trusted content digest.

findings.title: No replay fingerprint.
findings.detail: Current architecture requires checkpoints + acknowledgments + sequence cursors + replay fingerprints for reconnect/recovery; PCV-03 has no replay fingerprint binding restored history/state.

findings.title: Reconnect rendezvous is coupled to a new Campaign invitation.
findings.detail: The client can only establish a fresh WebRTC path by accepting another invitation offer. Membership invitation and transport rendezvous/resume should be separate after membership exists.

findings.title: Disconnect does not make host presence disconnected.
findings.detail: Closing the player's peer updates only local UI phase; no trusted host-side connection lifecycle updates presence.

findings.title: Presence messages are spoofable.
findings.detail: Host persistence trusts caller-supplied subject/device/status/timestamp rather than deriving identity and time from the bound transport connection.

findings.title: Presence time is client-authored.
findings.detail: `envelope.at` is accepted as the durable last-seen timestamp rather than host receipt time.

findings.title: Capability negotiation is an echo, not a client capability proof.
findings.detail: The host embeds pack/rules/epoch in the offer; the Android client copies those same values into the join request; the host compares them to itself.

findings.title: Joining device does not report locally measured installed pack/rules state.
findings.detail: It does not demonstrate that the required pack, exact rules profile/runtime version, or compatible schema is actually installed.

findings.title: Entitlement/grant compatibility from the canonical handshake is absent.
findings.detail: The current local/online Session contract calls for membership plus entitlement snapshot/grant digest/count/pack set/rules version/authority epoch/projection scope.

findings.title: PCV-02 exposes `rulesProfileVersion: "current"` into Session compatibility.
findings.detail: An immutable live Session must bind an exact resolved version/snapshot, not a moving symbolic version.

findings.title: Raw invitation secrets are persisted in ordinary Session JSON/SQLite.
Raw resume tokens are persisted in ordinary host and client document records.
findings.detail: Current security canon requires secrets to use an approved secret store; no secure-store adapter is used here.

findings.title: Secret generation fails open to `Math.random`.
findings.detail: If Web Crypto is unavailable, invitation/resume/private markers fall back to non-cryptographic randomness rather than failing closed.

findings.title: Wire envelopes are not actually decoded/validated.
findings.detail: `decodeWireEnvelope` checks only `kind` and casts arbitrary JSON to the union.

findings.title: No per-envelope protocol/schema version.
findings.detail: Unsupported major versions and unknown top-level fields cannot be rejected as required by serialization/versioning canon.

findings.title: No message size/depth/list/batch bounds.
findings.detail: A connected peer can send arbitrarily large JSON/payloads. No bounded-work/backpressure/rate contract exists.

findings.title: Malformed transport input is silently swallowed.
findings.detail: The transport catch block drops invalid input even though the comment claims the coordinator will return a role-safe protocol error.

findings.title: All major observations are emitted as literal `true` after weak structural checks.
findings.detail: The exporter does not record a causal proof receipt for each observation.

findings.title: Reconnect proof is only `connectionOrdinal >= 2`.
findings.detail: A second ordinary join can increment the ordinal and satisfy the evidence without a resume request succeeding.

findings.title: Idempotency proof does not prove a duplicate was attempted.
findings.detail: It checks uniqueness/count consistency of processed command IDs/receipts. One ordinary command can satisfy it.

findings.title: Ordered-delivery proof inspects host Event summary, not what Android actually received.
Installed Android runtime is host-trusted client metadata.
findings.detail: The Android join request self-reports `clientKind/clientRuntime/platform`; the evidence exporter later treats that as installed-runtime proof.

findings.title: Physical-device proof depends on one operator affirmation plus self-reported metadata.
findings.detail: There is no device-side receipt/artifact reference binding the Android installation and observed run to the package artifact.

findings.title: Verifier checks package `sourceHead` and platform set but not installed-binary identity.
findings.detail: It does not bind a device-side package hash/signature/version receipt to the exact artifact SHA-256 values.

findings.title: Evidence does not prove ACK-before-batch loss/recovery, stale authorization, invitation reuse, actor spoofing, or event-gap recovery.
findings.detail: The current focused tests are happy-path only.

findings.title: No migration/retirement path exists for `PCV-03.session.1`.
findings.detail: A repaired package using the same app data location can encounter old Session records containing raw invitation/resume credentials and stale parallel authority.

findings.title: Old unsafe records must not be silently upgraded into trusted new authority.
findings.detail: The safe repair should preserve only permitted non-secret audit/history references, retire/revoke old credentials/Sessions, and require fresh governed membership/session establishment under the new schema.

findings.title: PR #775 contains unrelated UI/skin work.
findings.detail: Showcase-skin plumbing, profile-drawer changes, Search/Notifications removal, and other presentation changes are mixed into the networking candidate. Valid work may be preserved on its owning completed/future surface, but it should not hitchhike as PCV-03 authority/transport repair.

findings.title: Prior archaeology wiring labels are too coarse for PCV-03
findings.detail: The project wiring matrix marked PCV-03 dimensions as audited/current-work without field-level owner-to-runtime proof; candidate-specific preflight must replace label-level assurance with concrete producer/owner/consumer evidence.
findings.candidate_resolution: Field-level authority/field/consumer/negative-regression matrix is defined by PCV-I06.

findings.title: PCV-02 Campaign membership representation is weaker than current A5 membership authority
findings.detail: ProductCampaignFoundation persists memberSubjectIds only, with no membership identity, role/state/version/delegation semantics; the interstitial must define a migration/adapter that preserves completed PCV-02 state without retaining two membership authorities.

findings.title: Logical campaign_members schema does not represent current A5 membership state/version semantics
findings.detail: The Phase-9 base table has campaign_member_id/campaign_id/subject_id/role/joined_at but no active/suspended/left/removed state or explicit version/update fields used by current A5 contracts.

findings.title: No production local StableSubjectSessionPort adapter exists
findings.detail: Only local-alpha/test adapters implement A3 stable-subject session behavior; the real product profile/identity store is not an A3 authentication-session implementation.

findings.title: No production local ProviderIndependentIdentityMapping adapter is wired
findings.detail: PCV-01 persists subjectId/identityId strings but the product does not instantiate the canonical provider-independent identity-mapping owner.

findings.title: Local product subject identity has no possession credential
findings.detail: No production local keypair, passkey, WebAuthn credential, or equivalent proof binds possession to the durable subject/identity IDs; zero-service multiplayer needs an explicit trust bootstrap before remote subject assertions can be authenticated.

findings.title: Stable device continuity has no explicit canonical owner/persistence contract
findings.detail: SMB-02 says device identity is connection context only, but there is no production device registry contract/schema that defines stable device binding, revocation, or relationship to an authenticated subject.

findings.title: BRP device-session management and revocation are not connected to product identity/session state
findings.detail: BRP-02 requires current/revoked device-session evidence and ordinary-user session management, but the PCV product profile has no corresponding production owner path.

findings.title: A5 membership state transitions are modeled but no public mutation seam exists
findings.detail: CampaignMembershipState includes active/suspended/left/removed, yet CampaignMembershipAndInvitationPort exposes issue/reissue/change-role/delegation but no suspend/leave/remove transition.

findings.title: A5 membership mutations do not carry explicit authentication-session or permission evidence
findings.detail: The public mutation inputs carry actorSubjectId but not the A3 authentication session / permission-decision references required by A5 security text; surrounding authorization ownership must be specified.

findings.title: A3 atomic invitation acceptance is not explicitly bridged to A5 Campaign membership persistence
findings.detail: InvitationPort promises one atomic membership+role transition, but the current public A3/A5 ports do not define the production transaction coordinator that creates/replays the A5 membership and returns its references.

findings.title: Campaign role vocabularies are not normalized across A5 and older P9 authorization
findings.detail: A5 uses game-master/assistant-gm/content-creator while the older Campaign authorization policy uses gm/player/observer; the supported translation/fail-closed rule must be explicit.

findings.title: SMB-01 production service-port layer is not connected to the local-first host profile
findings.detail: IdentityPort, EntitlementPort, PersistencePort, SessionCommandPort, RealtimePort and CheckpointPort have production-selected adapter plans, but no local-host adapters map PCV's zero-service execution to the same semantics.

findings.title: Selected SMB-01 server/Postgres authority and PCV local-host authority need an explicit composition rule
findings.detail: SMB-01 selects server-command/database authority for future production while PCV requires a GM installed-client executor when hosted services are inactive; both profiles need one owner model rather than contradictory authorities.

findings.title: LocalDocumentStore cannot express required cross-document atomic operations
findings.detail: The current get/put/delete document API has optimistic single-document revision checks but no transaction/batch/query seam for atomic invitation→membership→Campaign updates or multi-record lifecycle transitions.

findings.title: Relational logical schema and PCV JSON aggregate persistence are not explicitly mapped
findings.detail: The project has canonical Phase-9/A5 logical tables and the product has SQLite JSON documents; without a declared adapter/migration mapping they can become two durable truths.

findings.title: Device/resume/acknowledgment/authority-epoch/replay state lacks a durable-schema disposition
findings.detail: The logical schema has Sessions/commands/Events/projections/checkpoints but no explicit device-session, resume-token reference, ACK cursor, authority epoch or replay-fingerprint representation; each must be classified as canonical durable, local secret, or ephemeral connection state.

findings.title: Campaign invitation persistence has no secret-digest/reference field
findings.detail: A5 campaign_invitations stores recipient binding/state/expiry/operation identity but no bearer-secret digest or secure-store reference; the safe persistence strategy must be specified.

findings.title: No production secure-secret-store adapter is selected/wired
findings.detail: Invitation/resume/local identity credential material cannot remain ordinary LocalDocumentStore JSON, but the product currently has no approved secure-store abstraction/adapter.

findings.title: Manual signaling tokens themselves are sensitive secret/network material
findings.detail: Offer/answer tokens can contain bearer material and ICE/network metadata; they need explicit no-log/no-telemetry/no-durable-history handling and redaction rules.

findings.title: Pre-authorization signaling leaks protected Campaign/Session metadata
findings.detail: Current offers expose campaignId, sessionId, hostSubjectId, pack/rules data and projection scope before A3 recipient/auth checks; signaling must be inference-safe until authorization succeeds.

findings.title: Invitation lifetime and transport timeout values are magic policy
findings.detail: The candidate hard-codes a 24-hour invitation expiry and connection timeouts without a named current policy owner; policy values must be explicit/configurable and host-authoritative.

findings.title: Family-safety invitation policy is not integrated
findings.detail: MIB-17/SMB-14 can deny or require guardian approval for invitations; Campaign invitation/join must consume that product-policy decision without granting Campaign authority.

findings.title: Communication blocking/family policy interaction with peer establishment is undispositioned
findings.detail: SMB-14 governs communication blocking and family policy; the preflight must decide which peer/session communication capabilities it gates and at what stage.

findings.title: No production local entitlement adapter supplies the Session handshake
findings.detail: The canonical handshake expects entitlement/grant state and A3/A5 carry entitlement decision references, while PCV currently has no production local EntitlementPort implementation for the real product profile.

findings.title: Exact pack/rules capability identity is not resolved from symbolic PCV-02 state
findings.detail: PCV-02 stores rulesProfileVersion=current and a lightweight pack-lock reference; Session launch/handshake need exact immutable pack/rules/runtime/entitlement identity.

findings.title: Production Home/context path bypasses A3 authorized dashboard/context partitions
findings.detail: ProductProfile/ProductSelectedContext are read directly from productState, while A3 already defines authorization-safe workspace discovery, Personal Home and Campaign/Session context partitions.

findings.title: Remote Campaign/Session continuity needs an A3-safe product projection
findings.detail: Joined remote state should appear through authorized Campaign/Session context/Home references, not by copying host authority into the player's PCV-02 owner store or an ad hoc cache.

findings.title: Remote context cache partitioning and cross-context privacy are not connected
findings.detail: A3 provides subject/context cache partition keys and authorization evidence; PCV transport/product caches must not leak state between Campaign/Session contexts.

findings.title: SMB-01 outbox/realtime-advisory semantics are not mapped to direct WebRTC host execution
findings.detail: Production synchronization expects transactional outbox + durable sequence with realtime advisory; zero-service WebRTC needs an equivalent local-host durability/delivery mapping.

findings.title: Session command identity semantics are inconsistent across schema/runtime
findings.detail: The logical schema separates command_id and idempotency_key while the current generic handler effectively uses commandId as processed identity; the canonical mapping and payload fingerprint conflict rule must be fixed.

findings.title: Hidden global Event sequence versus viewer-visible delivery cursor is underspecified
findings.detail: Pre-publication filtering can omit global Event numbers, so reconnect/ACK logic needs separate authoritative stream/projection cursors rather than assuming visible contiguity.

findings.title: Checkpoint persistence lacks an explicit replay-fingerprint/trusted-digest contract
findings.detail: The logical checkpoint has checksum/state/revision while current recovery expectations also require replay fingerprints and an independently trusted digest/reference.

findings.title: MAS-16/MAS-17 depend on the same Session/Checkpoint/ActionEvent owners
findings.detail: Adventure Studio session-prep/playtest contracts bind to canonical Session, SessionCheckpoint and ActionEvent authority; the repaired PCV foundation must remain consumable without MAS becoming a parallel Session owner.

findings.title: APW hybrid live/async return depends on one Campaign/Session/Event history
findings.detail: Existing hybrid acceptance requires disconnect, async resolution, missed-event recovery and live resume on one authoritative history; PCV recovery contracts must preserve this future consumer.

findings.title: VTI is an explicit PCV-03 downstream compatibility target
findings.detail: VTI already has permissions/hidden-information/GM-authority and retry/result semantics; the base Session/transport contracts must preserve its adapter boundary without surfacing VTI product UI now.

findings.title: SAA-21 has its own multi-device collaboration lineage that must be classified
findings.detail: Sequential-art collaboration uses participant/device/project history and optional session lineage; preflight must decide whether it consumes generic transport primitives or remains a separate collaboration domain so authorities are not merged accidentally.

findings.title: WCI/MSAS/IC/A6/A7/A9 live-session consumers require compatibility disposition
findings.detail: Existing session-intelligence, sound/GM control, live-session UI, action, combat and noncombat contracts reference Session authority and must be mapped as downstream consumers without pulling their implementation into PCV-03.

findings.title: SMB-13 internal-alpha installation/join/evidence semantics must remain compatible
findings.detail: Remote internal-alpha productization already treats SMB-02 as remote Session authority and binds package/version/checksum/evidence; PCV certification must not create a competing distribution/join proof model.

findings.title: BRP recovery/data-rights obligations apply to device-session and secret lifecycle
findings.detail: Account recovery, ownership recovery, export/delete and privacy choices require a clear disposition for local identity credentials, device sessions, remote continuity and revocation data.

findings.title: Android API-37 local-network permission is a future packaging compatibility gate
findings.detail: Current APK targets SDK 36, so no new permission is required now; the target-SDK 37 upgrade must be recorded as a future compatibility trigger rather than forgotten or prematurely added.

findings.title: Secure-storage technology choice needs current platform verification
findings.detail: The preflight must select an approved Tauri-compatible secure local store for Windows and Android and record its version/platform/backup/export implications before secrets are moved.

findings.title: Application branch is content-restored but contains audit-only commit history
findings.detail: The premature red test was reverted and the branch content matches 8232e52 exactly; future implementation must create a new exact candidate and must not reuse the old package/evidence identity.
findings.candidate_resolution: PR #775 is closed unmerged; its branch, old exact candidate and package artifact are historical-only and forbidden as future PCV-03A candidate identity.

findings.title: Validation Core is still modeled as one monolithic PCV-03 application profile
findings.detail: ACTIVE_FAMILY_CONTRACT and profile PCV-03 do not understand PCV-I01..I06 or PCV-03A..03F; preflight must define bounded validation profiles so each future tranche validates only the contracts it can invalidate.
findings.candidate_resolution: PCV-03A..03F each receive a bounded validation-profile contract with explicit negative-regression ownership.

findings.title: Application validation currently auto-runs PCV-03 on substantive PR #775 changes
findings.detail: Because the application validation family still resolves PCV-03, contract-only interstitial changes in the app repo would be misclassified unless a dedicated preimplementation validation profile/branch strategy is established first.
findings.candidate_resolution: Each child starts from fresh application main and materializes/activates exactly one child profile; the obsolete monolithic PCV-03 candidate/profile is not reusable.

findings.title: Installed packaging is label-triggered and must remain disabled during preflight
findings.detail: package-pcv03 runs only on pcv03-package labeling; governance must explicitly keep packaging disabled until PCV-03F so obsolete installers are not rebuilt during contract/audit work.
findings.candidate_resolution: Application main has no PCV-03 packaging workflow; packaging creation/activation is forbidden in PCV-03A..03E and owned only by PCV-03F.

findings.title: Later live/async/hybrid mode transitions require a single stable authority history
findings.detail: SMB-02 and APW both prohibit mode changes from forking Campaign/Session/Event truth; local-host and eventual hosted profiles must share IDs/cursors/checkpoint semantics.

findings.title: Local identity recovery across device replacement/reinstall is unresolved
findings.detail: A device-held local credential can prove possession on one installation, but BRP requires account/ownership recovery without administrator/database intervention; preflight must define what survives, what can be exported, and what requires a new invitation/rebind.

findings.title: Invitation recipient binding design must distinguish proof-of-possession from device authority
findings.detail: The earlier opaque recipient-code concept can bootstrap a join, but it must bind an authenticated local subject credential and must not let the device ID itself grant Campaign identity/role.

findings.title: Manual WebRTC identity binding must include SDP/peer lifecycle without turning transport metadata into authorization
findings.detail: A successful DTLS/DataChannel connection proves transport continuity, not Campaign subject authority; the accepted A3/A5 subject must be bound to the peer context after authorization and revalidated on reconnect.

findings.title: StableSubjectSession omits assurance/device-label/last-validated authorization metadata from the A3 design
findings.detail: A3's original authentication-session model included authentication assurance, a non-fingerprinting device/client label, last validated permissions version and last validated entitlement version. The current StableSubjectSession record omits those fields, so remote/reconnect code has no canonical place to bind or invalidate them.

findings.title: IdentityServicePort does not define production-local proof-of-possession authentication
findings.detail: IdentityServicePort can create/get/link identities, while StableSubjectSessionPort establishes a session from an already asserted subjectId+identityId pair. No canonical production-local credential verification/issuance seam proves that a remote/local caller possesses that identity before session establishment.

findings.title: A5 participant projection omits the membership version required by its own role-change command
findings.detail: CampaignMembershipAndInvitationPort.changeMemberRole requires expectedVersion, but CampaignParticipantProjection exposes no version. A conforming caller cannot obtain the concurrency token from the same public boundary.

findings.title: Zero-service authoritative-host reachability is not defined for A3/A5 online gates
findings.detail: A3 invitation/workspace entry and A5 membership mutations require online=true, while PCV's approved zero-service model uses an installed GM host with no hosted backend. The contract must define online as reachability of the current authoritative executor/profile, not paid/cloud Internet availability.

findings.title: Current A5 membership representation loses parts of the original membership lifecycle contract
findings.detail: The original A3/Internal-Alpha membership model included scoped roles, effective/expiry times, granting authority, revocation and permissions version. Current A5 participant projection/base campaign_members schema does not preserve all of those fields; each must be intentionally retained, derived, or retired with evidence.

routing_rule: Each finding has exactly one primary closure interstitial, explicit secondary dependency families where material, and a future implementation destination. Cross-cutting dependencies never excuse duplicate owner authority.
